questions.question: Why do modern deep learning models require GPUs instead of standard CPUs?
options: CPUs lack support for floating point arithmetic
GPUs have thousands of parallel cores designed for matrix multiplication
GPUs have larger persistent storage drives
questions.explanation: Deep learning workloads are dominated by matrix operations (GEMM) that can be parallelized across thousands of small GPU cores simultaneously.

questions.question: What is the primary hardware bottleneck during autoregressive LLM token generation?
options: Network latency across cloud availability zones
Memory bandwidth (transferring weights from VRAM to compute cores)
questions.explanation: During autoregressive generation, weights must be transferred across the memory bus for each sequential token, making memory bandwidth the dominant constraint.

questions.question: As an AI TPM evaluating infrastructure, which question most directly challenges an over-provisioned GPU cluster proposal?
options: What color are the server chassis?
Have we benchmarked quantized weights (e.g. INT8/FP8) or smaller instances to verify if quality is retained at half the operational cost?
Can we rewrite the entire application in Assembly?
Why didn't we use 100% CPUs for training our 70B model?
questions.explanation: Quantization and rightsizing instances are high-impact TPM levers to reduce operational expenditure while preserving model output quality.
